territorial_scope.description: Applies to federal public bodies and the Executive, and requires state legislatures to harmonize their frameworks within a set period.

summary.short: Decree reforming, adding and repealing provisions of the Mexican Constitution to simplify public bodies. It extinguishes autonomous agencies including the Federal Competition Commission and the Federal Telecommunications Institute, moves competition and telecom regulation to the Executive, and reassigns data-protection oversight. In force the day after DOF publication.
summary.long: The decree reforms, adds and repeals provisions of Articles 3, 6, 26, 27, 28, 41, 76, 78, 89, 105, 113, 116, 123 and 134 of the Mexican Constitution. Article 6 A II sends competence over personal data held by private parties to the law under Article 90, and Article 6 A VIII subjects obligated bodies to a general transparency and data-protection law. Article 28 assigns telecommunications and broadcasting regulation and competition enforcement to the Executive, acting through its ministry and a competition authority. Article 134 requires public entities to eliminate duplicated functions and structures. Congress has ninety natural days from entry into force to adapt the relevant laws. The Federal Competition Commission and the Federal Telecommunications Institute are extinguished when the reformed Article 28 paragraphs take effect, 180 days after the secondary competition and telecommunications laws enter into force (Transitorio Décimo and Décimo Primero); other listed bodies, including the National Institute for Transparency, Access to Information and Personal Data Protection, the Energy Regulatory Commission and the National Hydrocarbons Commission, are extinguished when the secondary access-to-information law takes effect. Acts and contracts of extinguished bodies stay valid, and their staff's labour rights are preserved. The decree takes effect the day after DOF publication.

notes: Text is the DOF decree (Mexico City, 10 Dec 2024; promulgated 20 Dec 2024), not a consolidated constitution; only reformed, added and repealed provisions are reproduced, with unchanged text shown as ellipses. Internal inconsistencies: Transitorio Quinto makes the listed bodies extinct only after the secondary legislation of Transitorio Segundo enters into force, while Transitorio Décimo Primero extinguishes the CFCE and the IFT on entry into force of the Decree. Transitorio Quinto refers to the CNH, CRE and organismos garantes as public bodies covered by the Decree but does not expressly declare them extinct; Transitorio Sexto refers to the commissioners of the CRE and CNH. Transitorio Sexto also refers to the body in art. 3o., fracción IX, which the Decree repeals. The competition authority, the telecommunications and energy dependencies are described but not named. No other statutes are named, so no relations to them are coded. Transitorio Décimo sets a 180-day entry-into-force period for art. 28 paragraphs fifteen to twenty, counted from the secondary law.

obligations.summary: Obligated subjects must promote, respect, protect and guarantee the rights of access to public information and to personal data protection; the state laws set the bases and procedures for these rights.

thresholds.note: The decree sets no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. Its numbers are procedural time limits (ninety natural days in Transitorios Segundo and Cuarto, one hundred eighty days in Décimo), committee and body composition (cinco personas in Art. 41 Apartado A inciso a); two and three members), and dates; these are not coded as thresholds.

definitions.note: The decree defines no terms. Expressions that bear on scope, such as 'sujetos obligados' (Arts. 6o. and 116), 'agentes económicos' and 'insumos esenciales' (Art. 28), are used without a definition in this text.
